findings.reason: Untrusted source: hwsim_new_edge_nl is the doit handler for MAC802154_HWSIM_CMD_NEW_EDGE (registered in hwsim_nl_ops at lines 606-610 with .flags = GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM, so an unprivileged user in a user namespace holding CAP_NET_ADMIN there can issue it); the netlink attribute set is fully attacker-chosen. Violated invariant: the presence guard at lines 421-423 joins two negated presence tests with && instead of ||, so it returns -EINVAL only when BOTH MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_ID and MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_EDGE are absent; a message that includes RADIO_ID but omits RADIO_EDGE passes validation while info->attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_EDGE] stays NULL. The genl policy does not close the gap: hwsim_genl_policy (lines 579-583) declares [RADIO_EDGE] = { .type = NLA_NESTED } with no NLA_POLICY_REQUIRED/NLA_REJECT/required marker and the op sets GENL_DONT_VALIDATE_STRICT (line 607), so the genl core does not reject its absence. Unsafe use: the NULL slot is passed directly as the nesting attribute to nla_parse_nested_deprecated at line 425; that inline (include/net/netlink.h:1226-1233) calls nla_data(nla) = (char*)nla + NLA_HDRLEN and nla_len(nla) = nla->nla_len - NLA_HDRLEN (include/net/netlink.h:1137-1149) on the NULL pointer, giving a kernel NULL-pointer dereference oops (local DoS). A second, independent NULL deref path exists at line 431: v0 = nla_get_u32(info->attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_ID]) is executed with no covering presence check, so a message that supplies RADIO_EDGE but omits RADIO_ID also crashes (check-one-attribute-then-use-a-different-sibling). Counterevidence checked: lines 483-485 (hwsim_del_edge_nl) and 531-533 (hwsim_set_edge_lqi) in this same file already use the corrected || connective, i.e. the seed fix landed for those two handlers but hwsim_new_edge_nl was left with the inverted guard, which is exactly the variant relationship this intent searches for; no other presence check or policy-required coverage exists between the guard and the two uses.

limitations: Coverage is bounded to nested-parse/validate/for_each call sites whose nesting attribute is directly indexed from info->attrs[N]/tb[N]/attrs[N]/nla[N] (grep over all 336 helper call sites in net/, drivers/, fs/, kernel/ of snapshots/s02; every directly-indexed site was read together with its guard).

Call sites where the nesting attribute reaches the helper through an intermediate local or helper parameter (nf_tables_api.c expressions/elements lists, openvswitch flow_netlink.c actions, ip_tunnel_core.c, seg6_local.c, nexthop.c, lwt_bpf.c, pmsr.c, team.c, qeth, devlink, drbd_nla.c) were only spot-checked and are listed as unresolved candidates, not proven safe.

No compilation or reproducer was run: the snapshot tree is read-only and no top-level build was attempted; the NULL-deref conclusion rests on reading nla_parse_nested_deprecated (include/net/netlink.h:1226-1233) which calls nla_data(nla)/nla_len(nla) (1137-1149) on the passed attribute, and on the genl core not enforcing presence for a plain NLA_NESTED policy entry under GENL_DONT_VALIDATE_STRICT.

Privilege reachability is asserted from .flags = GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM (mac802154_hwsim.c:609), satisfiable by an unprivileged user with CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user namespace; whether the mac802154_hwsim module is loaded in a target configuration is deployment-dependent.
Impact is characterized as a local kernel NULL-pointer-dereference DoS (kernel oops) from unprivileged input; no privilege-escalation path was demonstrated.

The reported hwsim_new_edge_nl variant shares the seed's subsystem/file by construction of the snapshot pair; it is a different handler (NEW_EDGE vs the seed's DEL_EDGE) and this snapshot's DEL_EDGE/SET_EDGE instances carry the fix, but a reviewer applying a stricter same-subsystem exclusion rule should treat the two remaining unresolved candidate groups as the fallback scope.
